theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Consumer Staples (+0.76%) and Health Care (+0.14%) led the market today, while Technology (-6.97%) and Industrials (-3.18%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -3.87% versus +0.12% for defensives and -1.66% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -1.97% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -5.29%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up -2.80%, outperforming large caps. The VIX rose 26.06% to 35.89, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold added 0.17% to $3,539.00, crude oil was little changed at $83.62, and bitcoin slipped 0.03% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
